title: My heart went over to him
takeaway: Love can be the illness and the cure at the same time.
scene: The poet complains, half laughing, that his own heart has betrayed him. It left him and went to live with the beloved.

original: میرا دل ایہہ یارو بڑا بے وفا اے
ایہہ میرا سی ہوندا اوہدا ہو گیا اے
transliteration: Mera dil eh yaaro bara be-vafa ae
Eh mera si honda, ohda ho gaya ae
translation: Friends, this heart of mine is very disloyal.
It used to be mine, and now it's become his.
couplets.story: He tells his friends that his own heart is a traitor. It used to belong to him. Now it belongs completely to the beloved.

original: میری بیقراری نے مُل پا لیا اے
اوہدے قدماں اتے میرا سر پیا اے
transliteration: Meri beqaraari ne mull pa liya ae
Ohde qadmaan utte mera sir piya ae
translation: My restlessness has finally earned its reward:
my head now rests at his feet.
couplets.story: All those sleepless, restless nights paid off in the end. Now his head lies at the beloved's feet, which is where he wanted to be all along.

original: مٹائے پئی دنیا اوہنے نئیں مٹنا
محبت دا یارو جنہوں آسرا اے
transliteration: Mitaaye pai duniya, ohne nahin mitna
Mohabbat da yaaro jinhu aasra ae
translation: Let the world try to wipe him out; he won't be wiped out,
friends, the one who leans on love.
couplets.story: The world can try as hard as it likes to destroy someone. If that person is held up by love, they won't fall.

original: کوئی آیا تے ویندیاں ای لے گیا دل
میں تک رہیا ہو یا کیہ ماجرا اے
transliteration: Koi aaya te vendiyaan ee lai gaya dil
Main tak rahiya, hoya ki maajra ae
translation: Someone came and, just in passing, carried off my heart.
I'm left staring: what just happened?
couplets.story: Someone walked by and took his heart without even stopping. He's still standing there, stunned, trying to work out what happened.

original: ایہہ ویکھے تے تڑفے نہ دیکھے تے تڑفے
محبت دا روگ بڑا لا دوا اے
transliteration: Eh vekhe te tarfe, na dekhe te tarfe
Mohabbat da rog bara la-dawa ae
translation: It aches when it sees him, and it aches when it doesn't.
The sickness of love has no cure.
couplets.story: His heart hurts when it sees the beloved, and hurts when it doesn't. There's no way to win. Love is an illness that no medicine can fix.

original: بڑے چر دا چھڈ یا اجے نئیں جے مُکا
ایہہ یار وکدی زلف دا تذکرہ اے
transliteration: Bare chir da chhadiya, ajje nahin je mukka
Eh yaar vakdi zulf da tazkira ae
translation: I started long ago, and still it isn't finished:
this talk about my friend's curling hair.
couplets.story: He started talking about the beloved's beautiful curls a long time ago, and he still isn't done. He could go on forever.

original: وفا لے کے اپنی تیرے کول آیاں
میں ویکھاں تیرے کول کِنی جفا اے
transliteration: Vafa lai ke apni tere kol aayaan
Main vekhaan tere kol kinni jafa ae
translation: I've come to you bringing my loyalty.
Let's see how much cruelty you have for me.
couplets.story: He comes to the beloved with nothing but faithfulness. Go ahead, he says. Let's see how much unkindness you can give back. He'll still be loyal.

original: ایہہ اوہدی اے عادت اوہدی ادا اے
transliteration: Eh ohdi ae aadat, ohdi ada ae
translation: it's just his habit, just his way.
couplets.story: He ends with a joke on his own name. 'Tabassum' means 'smile'. So when people see him smiling through all this pain, they shouldn't be fooled. Smiling is just his habit. It's literally his name.

deeper: 'My head now rests at his feet' is the image of total surrender, which is the literal meaning of 'Islam'. For the seeker, losing your heart to God is not a defeat but the goal. 'The one who leans on love won't be wiped out' expresses trust in God (tawakkul): whoever relies on Him is protected, whatever the world does.
why: It's playful and sad at the same time, and it ends with a clever pun on the poet's own name.
prompt: Who or what do you lean on when the world feels like it's pushing against you?
notes: Couplet 6: 'vakdi zulf' is read as 'curling hair'.
